extracted.intended_audience: general readers of La Rochefoucauld; translators, editors, and Project Gutenberg distributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial/legal rules embedded in a Project Gutenberg edition of La Rochefoucauld's Maxims, covering transcription/translation conventions, edition selection, and Project Gutenberg redistribution/licensing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcribers' conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Spelling variants are preserved (e.g. labour instead of labor, criticise instead of criticize, etc.); the translators' comments are in square brackets [...] as they are in the text; footnotes are indicated by * and appear immediately following the passage containing the note (in the text they appear at the bottom of the page); and, finally, corrections and addenda are in curly brackets {...}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These explicit transcription conventions are stated at the start of the eBook and should be followed when producing or reusing this edition to preserve editorial transparency and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition / textual basis selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Maxims are printed from the edition of 1678, the last published during the author's life, and to this edition were added two Supplements (first: Maxims which had appeared in earlier editions and were afterwards omitted; second: additional Maxims found among the author's manuscripts). A third supplement of about fifty Maxims first published in 1692 is also included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the author's last corrected edition (1678) as the base text for 'the Maxims' and include the identified supplements (first, second, third) and the Reflections for a complete English edition as justified in the translators' preface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator collaboration principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted guidance: 'Translators should not work alone; for good Et Propria Verba do not always occur to one mind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translators are encouraged to collaborate (multiple readers/consultants) when rendering difficult or 'untranslatable' passages to better capture nuance and choose more fitting English phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation humility / fidelity goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The translators offer 'Some apology... to translate the untranslatable' and aim 'to do the Duc de la Rochefoucauld the justice to make him speak English.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge limits of translation, strive for fidelity to author's meaning and style, and explain editorial/translation choices (e.g., notes, introductions) to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of Reflections and supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: The present edition aims to give a complete English edition of Rochefoucauld's works as a moralist: the body of the work comprises the Maxims as the author finally left them, the first supplement (omitted maxims), the second (unpublished maxims from manuscripts), the third (50 added in 1692), and the Reflections, 'in which the thoughts in the Maxims are extended and elaborated,' now appearing in English for the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing an edition, include introductions, notes and the Reflections to provide fuller context rather than publishing the Maxims in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria / characteristics of good maxims (epigrammatic writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maxims are described as 'condensed good sense', 'short aphorism' with 'truth expressed in condensed sentences', and praised for being 'concise and energetic in expression, reduced to those short aphorisms which leave much to the reader's acuteness and yet save his labour' (Hallam). Voltaire and others stress precision, terseness, and concentrated expression of a central truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For composing or evaluating maxims/epigrams: aim for terseness, precision, concentrated truth, generalisation from experience, avoidance of pedantry, and an economy of expression that invites reader reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial authenticity / provenance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should be attentive to the history of prior editions: many earlier English editions were reprints of preceding ones 'without any regard to the alterations made by the author in the later editions published during his life-time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the author's last corrected edition (or clearly justified manuscript sources) over intermediate reprints; document provenance and editorial decisions (what was included/omitted and why).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include translators' notes, introduction, and contextual apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: This edition includes introduction, notes, and some account of the author and his times to aid understanding (translators expressly add introduction and notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanatory material (preface, introduction, notes, indices) when publishing classical texts to help readers situate and interpret the material.
